newsitem.title: USA: Monsanto says contempt of court claim dismissed.
newsitem.headline: Monsanto says contempt of court claim dismissed.

text.p: Monsanto Co said Wednesday a California Superior Court rejected a contempt of court claim against it made by Mycogen Corp as part of patent litigation between the two agriculture firms.

Mycogen had claimed that Monsanto was in contempt of court for not giving it the right to negotiate a license for certain germplasm related to herbicide-resistance in cotton, maize and oilseed rape and insect-resistance in maize.
Monsanto said it opposed the action on the basis that it allegedly was obligated only to grant Mycogen the right to negotiate a license for certain biotech genes.

"We had told Mycogen that we had fully performed our legal obligations and that the threat of a contempt action would not force us to supply Mycogen with valuable proprietary germplasm to which Mycogen is not entitled," David Snively, litigation counsel for Monsanto, said in a statement.

In a separate statement, Mycogen said that the court ruling did not reflect on the merits of its damage action relating to Monsanto's alleged failure to comply with terms of a contract to license certain genetic technology.
